title: Wall manifest, major 2 (DRAFT)
description: DRAFT until wave 4 builds it; nothing reads it before then. What one wall should show and how it should look: a time-anchored schedule, an optional scene overriding it, works to fetch ahead, and the wall's settings. The Player composes the mat itself, so works carry a device-independent master and a mat colour, not a composed render. Rules a schema cannot state (every referenced work is in works, slots do not overlap, the horizon is whole days) are in .prawduct/artifacts/player-contract.md § Major 2, and a document that breaks one is malformed.

playlist.description: What hangs on the wall: a theme until the rename, a playlist after.

settings.description: Set centrally for this wall, so nobody configures a Player to change them.

mode.description: Chosen from the modes this wall's Player reports it can do.

mat.description: The mat in inches on the wall, so the same numbers mean the same thing on any screen. The bottom takes width_inches times bottom_weight.

viewing_distance_m.description: How far a viewer stands, a fact about the room. The Player sizes label type from it and its own geometry.

works.description: Every work the schedule, the scene or staging names, keyed by work id. A Player never holds a reference it cannot resolve.

horizon.description: The span the slots cover, a whole number of days. After it ends with no fresh manifest, the Player replays the slots shifted by whole horizons.

slots.description: In time order, not overlapping, inside the horizon. A time no slot covers is dark.

scene.description: A live override, or null. While active it wins over the schedule; when until passes the wall returns to the schedule on its own. until null holds until released.

staging.description: Works to fetch and compose ahead, because a scene is being assembled. Nothing is shown because of this list.

instant.description: RFC 3339 with an offset. The pattern enforces it, because not every validator checks 'format'.

media.description: The presentation master: unmatted, device-independent, long edge capped.

url.description: Where to fetch it: a URI reference, resolved against the manifest's own URL. Today the server serves it at /media/sha256-<hex>; after a Library/Programming split it may name the Library's host, and no Player needs to change. The sha256 is the identity: the Player verifies the bytes against it, so a url that disagrees is caught at download and discarded.

label.description: The same label text as major 1.
